transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Out on the trails and even back in town, I keep hearing and sensing things from the landscape telling me what to do with my work, and it’s starting to scare me. It just feels so real, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Before these experiences started, did you have any recent medical illness or injury, or were you using alcohol, drugs, or new medications? When did this first begin?

No, I haven't had any medical illnesses, injuries, or issues with alcohol or drugs. Everything really started about nine months ago, right when I signed the lease and launched my dance studio full-time.

Since this began nine months ago, have the voices or messages stayed fairly consistent the whole time, or did they come on suddenly and change a lot from day to day? Have you also noticed other symptoms like your thoughts feeling jumbled, your speech becoming hard for others to follow, or your daily functioning dropping off?

The voices and messages actually only happened during my high, revved-up phase and stopped completely once I crashed. During that high period, my speech was so fast and disjointed that people couldn't follow me at all. Now, my daily functioning has totally tanked, leaving my studio in ruins and making basic tasks feel impossible.
During that high, revved-up period, did you also need much less sleep and feel unusually energetic, grand, or unstoppable? About how long did that phase last?

Yes, I barely slept at all and would stay up until dawn, but I felt completely unstoppable and convinced that my genius would make me an internationally famous choreographer. That intense, revved-up phase lasted for about two months before I crashed into this heavy, low period.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a distinct manic episode lasting about two months with markedly decreased need for sleep, increased energy, grandiosity, pressured/disorganized speech, and psychotic symptoms (hearing/messages from the landscape). The psychotic symptoms occurred during the elevated phase and resolved after the mood state changed, supporting bipolar affective disorder, current episode manic with psychotic symptoms rather than a primary psychotic disorder. There is also clear functional impairment and no evidence of substance or medical causation in the interview.
